transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, what really brought me in is that my mind just won't stay on one thing anymore. I work as a jeweler, and lately, when I'm at the bench, I'll jump from checking a customer email to looking at a saw mark, to hearing a noise outside... and then I realize I've completely lost track of the whole work order. It's just getting really hard to focus on what I'm supposed to be doing.
How long have you been noticing this trouble staying focused—did it start recently, or has it been a pattern for you going back to childhood?

No, it's not a childhood thing. It started pretty recently. Um... this whole wired, kind of out-of-control stretch really kicked off right after I got an award at a jewelry show. It went on like that for about two weeks.
During that two-week period after the award, how would you describe your mood—did you feel unusually happy, elated, or on top of the world, or more irritable and on edge than usual?

Honestly, it was kind of both. Right after the show, I felt... I don't know, just completely lit up. Like I was larger than life. But then it would flip, and I'd get really irritable. Like, if anyone asked me to just stick to normal shop hours or told me I needed to slow down, I just snapped right at them.

During that two-week period, did these mood changes actually stop you from doing your normal work or daily activities, or were you still able to function pretty much as usual despite feeling that way?

Well, it definitely stopped me from working normally. I actually missed a major custom delivery because I was so all over the place. And... my shop records got so completely disorganized that I had to just stop taking new work for now. It's been pretty bad. My family has even been checking in on me a lot more lately, just because they got worried about how far I'd slipped from my usual routines. So, yeah, I couldn't really function like I normally do.
Before this recent two-week period, have you ever had a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt persistently sad, low, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Well, yeah, actually... it's been happening the past couple of weeks. I just wake up with this really heavy, kind of hollow feeling. It's like... the shine has just completely gone out of everything. I don't really care about the work right now. Honestly, there have been a few mornings where I just sat in my truck and cried before I even tried to open up the shop.
During these past couple of weeks of feeling low, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Yeah... I have. I just keep having these thoughts that my family, and even my clients, would be better off if I wasn't around. I don't have a plan to actually do anything, but... it honestly scares me how often it comes up lately.
